title: Studio save goes live: two admins saving the same published object, the later save silently overwrites the earlier one (the published layer has no version a save can pin)
body:
repo:objectstack#2 · os-steve · session_01ADHkmRY38EZf38Yy3zthbY

Filed by the seat from #36511 (Studio Save/Cancel, save goes live), PR #36597 `## Acceptance notes` first bullet. Not claimed. Related: #36511.

Suggested-grade: p2
Suggested-domain: `domain:server` (the publish/save routes; the version field on the answer is a `domain:spec` widening that rides along)

## What happens

Before #36511 every Studio edit went to a draft, and the draft-version guard refused a second editor whose draft read was stale (conflict dialog: reload or overwrite). With save going live, a Save publishes and leaves no draft. Two admins who opened the same object with no pending draft both save: the later Save asserts "no draft" and succeeds, replacing the earlier editor's published change without a word. The server serves no version of the published layer that a save could pin.

## Ask

Restore the lost-update guard on the published layer, server side:
1. The single-item publish/save routes the Studio Save uses answer the published layer's version (an opaque token; the standard `ETag` header is the precedent, the existing draft-version guard is the in-repo one).
2. A save that names a stale version is refused with a typed conflict, and the Studio shows the same reload-or-overwrite dialog it shows for a stale draft today.
3. A save that names no version keeps today's behaviour (no narrowing of existing callers in this card).

Seat ruling on the interim (on #36511): no client-only re-read before save (it narrows the window but cannot close it); the window stays open until this card lands.

## Re-check

On main after this card: open one object in two sessions with no pending draft, save a change in each; the second save shows the conflict dialog instead of succeeding.
